1.1.text:
Article 6
(1) The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(2) The form of psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is that psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of care, nurturing, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.
(5) The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence of women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.

Article 13
In order to prevent violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the family:
a. protects women and children from various violations of rights within the household;
b. encourages the formation of a harmonious, educational, independent and responsible family; and
c. serves as a place of initial counseling and mediation for every family member who is suspected of experiencing violations of the rights of women and children.

Article 3
The regulation of protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to:
a. prevent violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. provide services to women and children victims of acts of violence; and
d. carry out empowerment of women victims of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Palembang.
2. City Government is the Government of the City of Palembang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Palembang.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the City Government.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Palembang.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the government to provide services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Act of Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
10. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
11. Reporter is a person, family, and community who sees and/or hears that an act of violence has occurred against a woman or any woman who becomes a victim of an act of violence by another person.
12. Protection of Women and Children in Conflict with the Law is a form of service that must be implemented by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and psychological to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror, and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and or examination in court hearings.
13. Protection .....
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Family Resilience is the dynamic condition of a family that has toughness and resilience and contains physical material and psychic mental spiritual capabilities to live independently and develop themselves and their family to live harmoniously in improving physical and spiritual welfare.
29. Community is a group of citizens who inhabit an official government administrative area (at the level of Neighborhood Association, Citizens Association, Village and Sub-district) and cooperate in life for a sufficiently long time and obey existing rules.
30. Religious Leaders consist of Ustadz/Ustadzah, Ulama, Pastors, Priests, Monks, Pedanda/Pandita/Sulinggih and other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity/awareness.
31. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery for victims of violence as determined in a decision of an authorized official.

Article 10
The family in efforts to protect the rights of women and children is responsible for:
a. protecting women and children from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women and children;
b. providing equal opportunities to women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. preventing the occurrence of violations against the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 9
(1) Participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence to the competent authorities.
(3) Supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
(4) Small group units in society consisting of religious scholars, intellectuals, and customary community units are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
(5) Community Participation referred to in paragraph (1) means that community responsibility is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 17
(1) Health services in handling women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (1) letter b for women and children victims of acts of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 hours, quality and conducted with maximum health service standards.
(2) Women and children victims of acts of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medico-legal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
(3) Medical services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims conducted by medical personnel and paramedics.
(4) Medico-legal services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b, constitute a form of medical service for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) Services .....

(2) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. counseling services;
b. provision of safe houses;
c. spiritual guidance; and
d. economic recovery.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be organized by:
a. UPT PPA is tasked with carrying out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children victims of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems;
b. the position of UPT PPA is under and responsible to the Head of the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection at the city level; and
c. religious institutions.

Article 16
(1) Complaints regarding acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of the victim, family, the community and/or community organizations.
(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) may be submitted by way of a complaint:
 a. directly or by direct findings;
 b. by telephone or the like; and
 c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions are also authorized to handle women and children victims of acts of violence obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services are regulated by the Mayor's Regulation.

Article 22
(1) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 20 paragraph (2) letter b, the City Government may provide a safe house for women and victims of acts of violence in the form of intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(2) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(3) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of violence who require a safe house include:
 a. their life is threatened;
 b. receiving rejection from family or community;
 c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and
 d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(4) Implementation .....

Article 12
In the framework of preventing violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the community:
a. actively participates in monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of the rights of women and children;
b. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevents the occurrence of unregistered marriages and child marriages.

Article 16
(1) Complaints regarding acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of the victim, family, the community and/or community organizations.
(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) may be submitted by way of a complaint:
 a. directly or by direct findings;
 b. by telephone or the like; and
 c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions are also authorized to handle women and children victims of acts of violence obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services are regulated by the Mayor's Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Palembang.
2. City Government is the Government of the City of Palembang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Palembang.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the City Government.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Palembang.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the government to provide services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Act of Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
10. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
11. Reporter is a person, family, and community who sees and/or hears that an act of violence has occurred against a woman or any woman who becomes a victim of an act of violence by another person.
12. Protection of Women and Children in Conflict with the Law is a form of service that must be implemented by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and psychological to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror, and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and or examination in court hearings.
13. Protection .....
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Family Resilience is the dynamic condition of a family that has toughness and resilience and contains physical material and psychic mental spiritual capabilities to live independently and develop themselves and their family to live harmoniously in improving physical and spiritual welfare.
29. Community is a group of citizens who inhabit an official government administrative area (at the level of Neighborhood Association, Citizens Association, Village and Sub-district) and cooperate in life for a sufficiently long time and obey existing rules.
30. Religious Leaders consist of Ustadz/Ustadzah, Ulama, Pastors, Priests, Monks, Pedanda/Pandita/Sulinggih and other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity/awareness.
31. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery for victims of violence as determined in a decision of an authorized official.

Article 17
(1) Health services in handling women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (1) letter b for women and children victims of acts of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 hours, quality and conducted with maximum health service standards.
(2) Women and children victims of acts of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medico-legal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
(3) Medical services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims conducted by medical personnel and paramedics.
(4) Medico-legal services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b, constitute a form of medical service for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) Services .....

(2) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. counseling services;
b. provision of safe houses;
c. spiritual guidance; and
d. economic recovery.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be organized by:
a. UPT PPA is tasked with carrying out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children victims of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems;
b. the position of UPT PPA is under and responsible to the Head of the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection at the city level; and
c. religious institutions.

Article 9
(1) Participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence to the competent authorities.
(3) Supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
(4) Small group units in society consisting of religious scholars, intellectuals, and customary community units are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
(5) Community Participation referred to in paragraph (1) means that community responsibility is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 6
(1) The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(2) The form of psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is that psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of care, nurturing, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.
(5) The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence of women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.

Article 3
The regulation of protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to:
a. prevent violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. provide services to women and children victims of acts of violence; and
d. carry out empowerment of women victims of violence.

Article 10
The family in efforts to protect the rights of women and children is responsible for:
a. protecting women and children from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women and children;
b. providing equal opportunities to women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. preventing the occurrence of violations against the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 22
(1) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 20 paragraph (2) letter b, the City Government may provide a safe house for women and victims of acts of violence in the form of intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(2) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(3) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of violence who require a safe house include:
 a. their life is threatened;
 b. receiving rejection from family or community;
 c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and
 d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(4) Implementation .....

Article 13
In order to prevent violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the family:
a. protects women and children from various violations of rights within the household;
b. encourages the formation of a harmonious, educational, independent and responsible family; and
c. serves as a place of initial counseling and mediation for every family member who is suspected of experiencing violations of the rights of women and children.

Article 6
(1) The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(2) The form of psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is that psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of care, nurturing, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.
(5) The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence of women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.

Article 16
(1) Complaints regarding acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of the victim, family, the community and/or community organizations.
(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) may be submitted by way of a complaint:
 a. directly or by direct findings;
 b. by telephone or the like; and
 c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions are also authorized to handle women and children victims of acts of violence obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services are regulated by the Mayor's Regulation.

Article 17
(1) Health services in handling women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (1) letter b for women and children victims of acts of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 hours, quality and conducted with maximum health service standards.
(2) Women and children victims of acts of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medico-legal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
(3) Medical services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims conducted by medical personnel and paramedics.
(4) Medico-legal services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b, constitute a form of medical service for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) Services .....

(2) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. counseling services;
b. provision of safe houses;
c. spiritual guidance; and
d. economic recovery.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be organized by:
a. UPT PPA is tasked with carrying out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children victims of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems;
b. the position of UPT PPA is under and responsible to the Head of the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection at the city level; and
c. religious institutions.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Palembang.
2. City Government is the Government of the City of Palembang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Palembang.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the City Government.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Palembang.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the government to provide services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household.
8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Act of Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
10. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
11. Reporter is a person, family, and community who sees and/or hears that an act of violence has occurred against a woman or any woman who becomes a victim of an act of violence by another person.
12. Protection of Women and Children in Conflict with the Law is a form of service that must be implemented by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and psychological to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror, and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and or examination in court hearings.

27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Family Resilience is the dynamic condition of a family that has toughness and resilience and contains physical material and psychic mental spiritual capabilities to live independently and develop themselves and their family to live harmoniously in improving physical and spiritual welfare.
29. Community is a group of citizens who inhabit an official government administrative area (at the level of Neighborhood Association, Citizens Association, Village and Sub-district) and cooperate in life for a sufficiently long time and obey existing rules.

Article 6
(1) The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.

In order to prevent violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the family:
a. protects women and children from various violations of rights within the household;
b. encourages the formation of a harmonious, educational, independent and responsible family; and
c. serves as a place of initial counseling and mediation for every family member who is suspected of experiencing violations of the rights of women and children.

Article 10
The family in efforts to protect the rights of women and children is responsible for:

c. preventing the occurrence of violations against the rights of women and children in the household.

In the framework of preventing violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the community:
a. actively participates in monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of the rights of women and children;
b. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevents the occurrence of unregistered marriages and child marriages.

(4) The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of care, nurturing, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women and children is responsible for:
a. protecting women and children from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women and children;
b. providing equal opportunities to women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. preventing the occurrence of violations against the rights of women and children in the household.

(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

(5) The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence of women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women and children is responsible for:
a. protecting women and children from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women and children;
b. providing equal opportunities to women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. preventing the occurrence of violations against the rights of women and children in the household.

a. protects women and children from various violations of rights within the household;

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Palembang.
2. City Government is the Government of the City of Palembang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Palembang.

8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Act of Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
10. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
11. Reporter is a person, family, and community who sees and/or hears that an act of violence has occurred against a woman or any woman who becomes a victim of an act of violence by another person.
12. Protection of Women and Children in Conflict with the Law is a form of service that must be implemented by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and psychological to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror, and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and or examination in court hearings.

27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Family Resilience is the dynamic condition of a family that has toughness and resilience and contains physical material and psychic mental spiritual capabilities to live independently and develop themselves and their family to live harmoniously in improving physical and spiritual welfare.
29. Community is a group of citizens who inhabit an official government administrative area (at the level of Neighborhood Association, Citizens Association, Village and Sub-district) and cooperate in life for a sufficiently long time and obey existing rules.

Article 6
(1) The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(2) The form of psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is that psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of care, nurturing, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.
(5) The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence of women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.

b. providing equal opportunities to women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. preventing the occurrence of violations against the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 6
(1) The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(2) The form of psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is that psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, sexual intercourse in an unnatural manner or not desired by one of the parties, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of care, nurturing, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.
(5) The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence of women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.
